newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close little changed.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close little changed.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed almost unchanged on Tuesday as even the publishing of several positive earnings reports failed to cheer the market, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.04 percent, or 0.07 points, to 192.50 on a low all-share turnover of 48 million shekels against 53 million on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.04 percent to 202.29.
"Activity is low and the market is asleep. Even the publishing of several good earnings reports did not affect trading," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeler Eblagon Securities.
"The market was indifferent to those reports and trading continued to be very sluggish," Eidelheit added.
Elbit rose 2.0 percent to 12,738 after it reported third-quarter net profit of $3.567 million, compared with $3.310 million in the year-earlier period.
Super Sol gained 1.25 percent to 7,431 after reporting third-quarter net profit rose to 28.5 million shekels from 23.6 million a year earlier.
Dead Sea Works closed unchanged at 819 after it reported third-quarter net profit of 35 million shekels against 31.4 million at the same period last year.
Dead Sea's parent Israel Chemicals gained 0.75 percent to 274.
Bezeq Israel Telecom, the second-most active share, fell 2.5 percent to 775 on volume of 2.3 million shekels after Ofek Securities rated the company as "underperform".
"Trading was mixed and selective but activity was very low. Even the publishing of positive earnings reports had no real impact on trading," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
The most active share was Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 2.0 percent to 146,241 on volume of 5.6 million shekels.
Clal Industries rose 1.75 percent to 1,320 on volume of 1.9 million shekels.
